linkages: Employment spells linked to employers via firm (legal-unit) identifiers in BFL; an employer is a legal unit that can own many establishments, so EE transitions are transitions between different firms and not establishments.
Transitions arising from changes in firm identifiers due to split-ups, mergers, etc. are corrected.
The daily spell panel is collapsed to monthly and quarterly panels to mimic datasets without daily information (e.g. the US LEHD).

sample.universe: All persons in Denmark having a job from age 18 to 60, 2008-2019; BFL records the universe of employment spells at the monthly level with exact daily start and end dates since 2008.
sample.unit_of_observation: Worker-year observations in the descriptive statistics; worker-period job spells and job-to-job transitions in the misclassification analysis; quarterly aggregate time-series observations in the Table 1 / Table A.3 regressions.
selection_rules: All employment spells recorded in BFL from 2008 onwards (public and private employers).
Exclude workers below age 18 and above age 60.
Daily EE definition: allow up to seven days of non-employment between employment spells.
Quarterly / monthly "adjacent" definition: two different employers in two adjacent periods.
Quarterly "within" definition: different employers within the same quarter.
Correct transitions due to changes in firm identifiers from split-ups, mergers, etc.
Exclude hires and separations from recalls, and transitions into and out of the dataset.
Exclude mobility between establishments, within a business group, and within an establishment (this version of the paper).

Earnings-difference analysis: restrict to transitions for which multiple quarters are observed in both the origin and destination firms; earnings levels are used for the remaining single-quarter spells.
Table 2 / algorithm sample: condition on observing two quarters in order to take differences, deleting the first and last quarter of the sample.
sample.period: 2008-2019 (Table A.1 reports the sample as 2008Q2 to 2019Q3)
sample.n_observations: 44,597,537 worker-year observations (Tables A.1 and A.2); 46 quarterly observations in the Table 1 and Table A.3 regressions; Table A.4 group sizes: 1,922,901 multi-quarter and 1,639,324 single-quarter within transitions, 876,066 multi-quarter and 1,568,908 single-quarter adjacent-without-within transitions.
sample.n_individuals: 3,691,325 workers; 326,786 firms; 417,765 establishments; 2,092,942 employees in cross-section (Table A.2)

construction_notes: Daily spells are collapsed to lower frequencies: if a worker is employed just one day within a period (month/quarter) this is recorded as employment in that period, and earnings are aggregated for each employer within each period.
Daily EE transitions allow seven days of non-employment between employment spells, following Bertheau et al. (2020).
Four main measures of EE transitions: (i) daily, (ii) monthly "adjacent", (iii) quarterly "adjacent", (iv) quarterly "within".

Earnings difference in the origin firm = earnings in t_o minus earnings in t_o-1, where t_o is the last quarter in the origin firm; earnings difference in the destination firm = earnings in t_d minus earnings in t_d+1, where t_d is the first quarter in the destination firm.
The cyclical indicator in Table 1 is the deviation from the HP filtered trend of the unemployment rate; in Table A.3 it is the change in the unemployment rate.
Error rates in Figs. 4, 5 and A.3 are computed per percentile bin as errors divided by transitions in the bin; error rates in Table 2 are errors divided by the total number of true EE transitions.
Average hourly wage is reported in real DKK (207.9 in Table A.1).
Thresholds for the correction algorithm are reported in Appendix Table A.6, both symmetric (k_.,.,o = 1 - k_.,.,d) and unrestricted.

key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in Section 2.1, following Bertheau et al. (2020).
